definitions.explanation: An honorific term for someone's death, used to show respect for the deceased. Commonly used in formal announcements, obituaries, and news reporting about notable people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{逝去|せいきょ}⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
{享年|きょうねん}{八十五|はちじゅうご}⟦{歳|さい}→歳：10017_sai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{逝去|せいきょ}⟦されました→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He passed away at the age of eighty-five.

examples.japanese: ⟦{著名|ちょめい}→著名：13992_chomei⟧な⟦{作家|さっか}→作家：01414_sakka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{逝去|せいきょ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{悼|いた}み→悼む：12622_itamu⟧、⟦{各地|かくち}→各地：00155_kakuchi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{追悼|ついとう}{式|しき}→追悼式：24788_tsuitoushiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: Memorial services were held across the country to mourn the passing of the renowned author.

notes:
USAGE:
{逝去|せいきょ} is an honorific (respectful) term for death. It elevates the deceased and should not be used when referring to one's own family members' deaths (use ⟦{亡|な}くなる→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧ instead) or in casual conversation.

REGISTER:
This word belongs to formal/respectful register. In descending formality:
- {逝去|せいきょ} (honorific, for respected persons)
- ⟦{死去|しきょ}→死去：13240_shikyo⟧ (neutral-formal, news reporting)
- ⟦{亡|な}くなる→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧ (standard polite)
- ⟦{死|し}ぬ→死ぬ：00669_shinu⟧ (plain/blunt)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {逝去|せいきょ}⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧ (to pass away — honorific form)
- {逝去|せいきょ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{知|し}らせ→知らせ：03252_shirase⟧ (news of someone's passing)
- ご{逝去|せいきょ} (passing — with honorific prefix)

Often seen in the set phrase ご{逝去|せいきょ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{悼|いた}み→悼む：12622_itamu⟧ (mourning the passing of...).
